source: Marqu - The Hebrew Gospel of Mark v1.2
note: Verses 3-5 appear merged in the source text (v3 contains content from v4-5). The colophon at end of v20 reads: 'Here end the chapters of Matthew 54 and the chapters of Mark 16.'

verses.translation: And when the Shabbat{H7676} had passed{H5674}, Miryam{H4813} of Magdala and Miryam{H4813} the mother{H517} of Ya'aqov{H3290} and Shlomi bought{H7069} costly{H4030} ointment{H4888}, in order to anoint{H4886} Yeshua{H3442}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses משיחה מרגליית (meshichah margaliit — 'costly ointment', H4888+H4030). The word משיחה is from the same root as משיח (mashiach — 'Messiah/Anointed'). The women come to 'anoint' (למשוח) the Anointed One (משיח). This wordplay is visible only in Hebrew. Greek ἀρώματα ('spices') has no connection to Christos.
translation_notes: The mashiach/meshichah wordplay: women bring anointing-oil (משיחה) to anoint (למשוח) the Anointed One (משיח).

verses.translation: And they came{H935} to visit{H1239} in the morning{H1242}, the day after, at the tomb{H6913}, and the sun{H8121} had already come out{H3318}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses לבקר (levaqer — 'to visit/inspect', from H1239 baqar). Greek ἔρχονται ('they come'). Hebrew adds a specific PURPOSE — an inspection visit. A back-translator would use באו alone.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'the day after, in the morning.' Greek: λίαν πρωΐ ('very early'). Hebrew uses מחרת — a specific time reference.

verses.translation: And they said{H559} among themselves: Who{H4310} shall roll{H1556} for us the stone{H68} at the tomb{H6913}? They saw{H7200} sitting{H3427} at the right{H3225} side — a certain young man{H5288} clothed{H3847} in a white{H3836} garment{H899} — and they were afraid{H6342}.

one_way_hebrew: The source text merges Greek vv3-5 into a single verse. The women's question about the stone, seeing the young man, and their fear are compressed — a different narrative structure than the Greek.
greek_deviations: Hebrew compresses Greek vv3-5 into one unit. Greek separates these into distinct sequential actions (asking about stone, seeing it rolled, entering tomb, seeing young man).

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Do not fear{H6342}! You sought{H1245} Yeshua{H3442} the Nazarite{H5139} who was hung{H8518}. He is not here{H6311}. See{H7200} this place{H4725} where they placed{H3240} him.

one_way_hebrew: Uses שנתלה (shenitlah — 'who was hung', from H8518 talah). Greek ἐσταυρωμένον ('the crucified one'). Consistent Torah hanging vocabulary throughout Mark.
Uses נצרי (natsri — 'the Nazarite') — the triple-wordplay title (consecrated one / branch / Nazareth). Greek Ναζαρηνόν captures only geography.
greek_deviations: Greek adds ἠγέρθη ('he is risen') — the explicit resurrection statement. Hebrew says only איננו פה ('he is not here'). The Hebrew is more enigmatic — absence rather than explicit resurrection.

verses.translation: Go{H1980} immediately to the disciples and to Kefa and say{H559} to them that he goes before{H6440} them to the Galil{H1551} — there you shall see{H7200} him, as he said{H559} to you.

one_way_hebrew: Uses תכף (tekhef — 'immediately'). Greek has no equivalent urgency word. The Hebrew adds immediacy absent from Greek.

verses.translation: And they went out{H3318} and fled{H1272} from the tomb{H6913}, for their dread{H6343} was great{H1431}, and they trembled{H7460}; and to no{H3808} man{H120} did they say{H559} a thing{H1697}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses פחדתן (pachadtan — 'their dread', from H6343 pachad). This is the same word as פחד יצחק ('the Fear/Dread of Isaac', Gen 31:42,53) — a divine terror. Greek τρόμος και ἔκστασις ('trembling and astonishment'). The Hebrew echoes the patriarchal encounter with the divine.
textual_notes: Many scholars consider the original Greek Mark to end here at v8. The Hebrew continues with vv9-20.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442}, when he returned{H7725} alive{H2416} on the first{H7223} day{H3117} in the morning{H1242}, appeared{H7200} first{H7223} to Miryam{H4813} of Magdala, from whom he had driven out{H1644} seven{H7651} demons{H7700}.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: Uses חזר חי (chazar chai — 'returned alive', H7725+H2416). Greek ἀναστάς ('having risen'). Hebrew does NOT use a resurrection verb. It says he 'RETURNED ALIVE' — went away (died) and came back (alive). A back-translator from ἀναστάς would use קם ('rose') or נעור ('awakened'), NOT חזר חי.
Uses גורש (gorash — 'drove out/expelled', H1644) — the verb for expelling Adam from Eden (Gen 3:24) and driving out the Canaanites (Ex 23:28-31). Greek ἐκβεβλήκει ('had cast out') is more generic.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'returned alive' (חזר חי). Greek: 'having risen' (ἀναστάς). Return vs. resurrection.
translation_notes: 'Returned alive' for chazar chai — framing death as departure and resurrection as return.

verses.translation: And she went{H1980} and told{H5046} the others who had been with Yeshua{H3442}, who were standing{H5975} grieving and sighing{H585} and weeping{H1058} and groaning.

one_way_hebrew: Uses FOUR grief terms: אנונים ('grieving'), אנוחים ('sighing', H585), בוכים ('weeping', H1058), מתאנחים ('groaning'). Greek has only πενθοῦσιν και κλαίουσιν ('mourning and weeping' — TWO terms). A back-translator would not expand two Greek terms to four Hebrew ones.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: four grief terms. Greek: two grief terms.

verses.translation: They who heard{H8085} that he had returned{H7725} alive{H2416}, that she had seen{H7200} him, did not believe{H539}.

one_way_hebrew: Again חזר חי ('returned alive') — consistent with v9.

verses.translation: And after this, he appeared{H7200} to two{H8147} disciples who were going{H1980} to a certain city{H5892}, in the form{H6755} of strangers{H1616}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses בצורת גרים (b'tsurat gerim — 'in the form of strangers/sojourners', H6755+H1616). Greek ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ ('in another form'). Hebrew specifies גרים (gerim — 'resident aliens') — the OT category from Gen 23:4, Lev 19:33-34. The risen Yeshua appears as a ger — an alien in his own land, echoing Abraham's self-description (Gen 23:4). A back-translator from 'another form' would NOT specify 'strangers.'
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'in the form of strangers' (specific identity). Greek: 'in another form' (vague transformation).

verses.translation: And they went{H1980} and told{H5608} the other{H312} disciples, and they did not believe{H539}.

And after the first{H7223} day{H3117}, when all{H3605} eleven were sitting{H3427} at table to eat{H398}, Yeshua{H3442} appeared{H7200} to them, to reproach their refusal and the hardness{H7186} of their heart{H3820}, for they had not believed{H539} those who saw{H7200} him when he returned{H7725} alive{H2416}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses מיאונם ('their refusal') — active refusal. Greek ἀπιστίαν ('unbelief'). Hebrew specifies willful refusal; Greek names a state.
Third use of חזר חי ('returned alive') for the resurrection.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'after the first day' (specific timing). Greek: ὕστερον ('afterward', vague).

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Go{H1980} into all{H3605} the world and proclaim{H1875} the word{H1697} of the King{H4428} of Heaven{H8064} to every{H3605} creature{H1254}.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: Uses דבר מלך השמים (dvar melekh hashamayim — 'the word of the King of Heaven'). Greek τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ('the gospel'). The Hebrew uses a ROYAL DECREE metaphor — the message is a king's edict. A back-translator from 'gospel' would use בשורה ('good news'), NOT 'the word of the King of Heaven.'
Uses דרשו (dirshu — 'proclaim/seek', from H1875 darash). Root of מדרש (midrash). Greek κηρύξατε ('preach/herald'). A back-translator would use קראו or הכריזו, not darash.
Uses בריה (beriyah — 'creature', from H1254 bara — 'to create'). The Genesis 1 creation verb.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'the word of the King of Heaven' (royal decree). Greek: 'the gospel' (good news). Different metaphors.

verses.translation: The one who believes{H539} and is immersed{H2881} shall be saved{H3467}, and the one who does not believe{H539} shall be blotted out{H4229}.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: Uses ימחה (yimmacheh — 'shall be blotted out', from H4229 machah). This is the verb for blotting names from the Book of Life (Ex 32:32-33, Deut 9:14, 25:19, Ps 69:28). Greek κατακριθήσεται ('shall be condemned'). A back-translator would use יורשע ('condemned'), NOT the Book of Life erasure verb.
Uses טבול (tavul — 'immersed', from H2881 taval — 'to dip'). The OT verb for ritual immersion (Lev 14:6,16; 2 Kgs 5:14 — Naaman's immersion).
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'blotted out' (ימחה, Book of Life). Greek: 'condemned' (κατακριθήσεται, legal). Erasure vs. judgment.
translation_notes: 'Blotted out' for yimmacheh — the Book of Life erasure verb, not mere condemnation.
'Immersed' for tavul — the OT ritual dipping verb.
textual_notes: Exodus 32:32-33 — 'blot me out (מחני) of your book... whoever has sinned, him will I blot out (אמחנו).'

verses.translation: And these wonders{H6381} shall those who believe{H539} perform: they shall heal{H7495} in my name{H8034} the demon-possessed, and they shall speak{H1696} diverse{H2487} tongues{H3956}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses ירפאו ('shall heal', H7495 rapha). Greek ἐκβαλοῦσιν ('shall cast out'). Hebrew: HEAL the demonized. Greek: CAST OUT the demons. Different approach — healing a person vs. expelling an entity.
Uses חלוף לשונות ('diverse/changed tongues', H2487+H3956). Greek γλώσσαις καιναῖς ('new tongues'). Hebrew: 'changed tongues' (transformed). Greek: 'new tongues' (additional).
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'heal the demon-possessed.' Greek: 'cast out demons.'

verses.translation: No{H3808} manner of beasts{H929} or venomous serpents{H5175} shall harm{H5142} them, and they shall lay{H3240} hands{H3027} on the sick{H2470} and they shall be healed{H7495}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses בהמות ונחשים ('beasts and serpents'). Greek mentions only ὄφεις ('serpents') and θανάσιμόν ('deadly poison'). Hebrew adds בהמות (behemot — 'beasts', H929) — the Genesis 1:24-25 and Job 40:15 word — absent from Greek.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'beasts and venomous serpents.' Greek: 'serpents and deadly poison.'
textual_notes: Genesis 3:15 — 'He shall crush your head, and you shall bruise his heel.' Victory over the serpent extends to believers.

verses.translation: And our lord{H113} Yeshua{H3442} the Anointed{H4899}, after he spoke{H1696} to them, went up{H5927} to the heavens{H8064} and sits{H3427} at the right hand{H3225} of the Name{H8034}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses לימין השם (limin hashem — 'at the right hand of the Name'). Greek ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ('at the right hand of God'). Hebrew uses the reverential circumlocution 'the Name.' A back-translator would use אלהים, not the Jewish substitute.
Uses משיח (mashiach — 'Anointed', H4899) — the native Hebrew title. Greek Χριστός is the translation of this.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'right hand of the Name.' Greek: 'right hand of God.' Reverential circumlocution vs. direct naming.
textual_notes: Psalm 110:1 — 'YHWH said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand (שב לימיני).' The ascension fulfills the Psalm.

verses.translation: And they went{H1980} into all{H3605} the world to proclaim{H1875} with the help{H5828} of the Name{H8034}, with good{H2896} words{H1697} and with wonders{H6381} that they performed.

one_way_hebrew: Uses בעזר השם (b'ezer hashem — 'with the help of the Name') — a standard Jewish invocation formula still used today. Greek τοῦ κυρίου συνεργοῦντος ('the Lord working with them'). The Hebrew uses the liturgical formula; the Greek describes cooperation. A back-translator would not produce בעזר השם.
Uses דברים טובים (devarim tovim — 'good words', H1697+H2896). Greek τὸν λόγον βεβαιοῦντος ('confirming the word'). Different descriptions of apostolic activity.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'with the help of the Name' (Jewish formula). Greek: 'the Lord working with them.'
Hebrew: 'good words and wonders.' Greek: 'confirming the word with signs.'
textual_notes: The colophon reads: 'Here end the chapters of Matthew 54 and the chapters of Mark 16.' This confirms the manuscript's self-awareness as part of a canonical collection.

chapter_notes.summary: Mark 16 in Hebrew presents the resurrection and commissioning with several distinctive one-way markers. The most striking: (1) חזר חי (chazar chai — 'returned alive') used THREE times (vv9,11,14) instead of any resurrection verb — framing death as departure and resurrection as return; (2) דבר מלך השמים (v15) — 'the word of the King of Heaven' where Greek has 'the gospel,' a royal-decree metaphor; (3) ימחה (v16) — 'shall be blotted out' (Book of Life erasure from Ex 32:32-33) where Greek has 'condemned' — ontological erasure vs. legal judgment; (4) בצורת גרים (v12) — Yeshua appears 'in the form of strangers' (the OT sojourner category) where Greek has 'in another form'; (5) בעזר השם (v20) — the Jewish prayer formula 'with the help of the Name'; (6) the mashiach/meshichah wordplay in v1; (7) four grief terms (v10) vs. Greek's two; (8) ירפאו (v17) — 'heal' the demonized vs. Greek 'cast out' demons; (9) consistent השם ('the Name') as reverential circumlocution. The chapter colophon confirms the manuscript's self-awareness as part of a canonical collection.
